project.name: NetLens
project.summary: NetLens is a multi-module Kotlin Android diagnostics app with Compose tools and a Glance home-screen widget. It runs probes on the device, keeps history and inventory in Room, and uses WorkManager for widget refresh and saved-network device watch.

nodes.label: Device and repository scripts
nodes.summary: Verifies widget rendering with ADB, checks store copy and hooks repository indexing.

nodes.label: WHOIS registries
nodes.summary: Provide registration records through IANA bootstrap and referred WHOIS servers.

nodes.label: Address intelligence tests
nodes.summary: Covers address lookup, registry handling and subnet calculations.

nodes.label: Build and device tooling
nodes.summary: Defines the Gradle project and provides baseline profile and device verification utilities.

nodes.label: Network security diagnostics tests

files.name: Tool destination
s: What a tool's `query` navigation argument holds.

files.name: Tool query
s: Vets the `query` argument one tool hands to another before it becomes a navigation route.

files.name: Android screenshot convention plugin
s: Composition smoke tests for Compose screens, via Paparazzi.

files.name: Fake data store
s: In-memory [DataStore] of [Preferences], for testing anything built on `UserPreferencesRepository` — which takes an injectable `DataStore` precisely so it can be faked on the JVM (there is no Robolectric in this repo,…

files.name: Fake device identifier dao
s: In-memory [DeviceIdentifierDao] honouring the real contracts: `UNIQUE(kind, value, scopeKey)` makes [insertIfNew] return -1, and [rescope] is `UPDATE OR IGNORE` (0 rows on a collision).

files.name: Fake key value store
s: In-memory [KeyValueStore] mirroring `EncryptedKeyValueStore`'s blank handling: reading a blank value yields null, and writing a null or blank value removes the key rather than storing it.

files.name: Fake known device dao
s: In-memory [KnownDeviceDao] that reproduces the real DAO's observable behaviour.

files.name: Fake network event dao
s: In-memory [NetworkEventDao] that actually applies the filters it is asked for.

files.name: Fake network key alias dao
s: In-memory [NetworkKeyAliasDao]; `aliasKey` is the primary key, so a second insert returns -1.

files.name: Fake data store test
s: Pins the two properties a consumer actually relies on: writes are visible to later reads, and `data` is a live flow rather than a one-shot snapshot.

files.name: Fake device identity dao test
s: Mirrors the transactional cases of core:data's `DeviceIdentityDaoTest` against the fake.

files.name: Fake identity daos test
s: Pins each identity fake to the contract the real DAO is tested against in core:data's `DeviceIdentityDaosTest` (same inputs, same asserted values), plus the REPLACE / trim / alias gaps.

files.name: Fake key value store test
s: Pins the blank handling, the one part of this fake that could drift weaker than `EncryptedKeyValueStore`.

files.name: Fake known device dao test
s: Four separate `KnownDeviceDao` doubles existed before this one and had drifted apart.

files.name: Fake known device guarded save test
s: Mirrors core:data's `KnownDeviceGuardedSaveTest` and the union-merge cases against the fakes.

files.name: Fake network event dao test
s: `:feature:wifiaudit` carried a copy of this fake whose every query method returned `flowOf(inserted.take(limit))` — the type, from and to arguments were accepted and thrown away.

files.name: Ssrf redirect probe
s: A [MockEngine] that answers the first request with a 302 into a private address, and records whether anything ever actually followed it.

files.name: Display text
s: Flattening for network-supplied strings that get rendered into a delimited format.

files.name: Host name
s: Validation for host strings that did not come from the user.

files.name: Network selector
s: Transport flags of one enumerated network, snapshotted so selection stays JVM-testable.

files.name: Fake device discovery pipeline
s: Scripted [DeviceDiscoveryPipeline]: replays [events] in order for every [run].

files.name: Fake lan network binder
s: Records whether the process was "bound" while a block ran.

files.name: Fake oui lookup
s: Vendor lookup keyed by **OUI prefix**, the way the real one is.

files.name: Inventory fakes
s: Every in-memory DAO the inventory repository needs, wired around the caller's [known] fake so a test can assert on the same instance it hands to a ViewModel.

files.name: Fake oui lookup test
s: A test double is only useful if it is no weaker than the thing it stands in for.

files.name: Fake port scanner test
s: A test double is only useful if it is no weaker than the thing it stands in for — the same rule [FakeOuiLookupTest] pins for its fake.

files.name: Device identifier recorder
s: Write path for identifiers of a device that already has an id.

files.name: Device identity resolver
s: Decides which known-devices row each scanned device is.

files.name: Identity policy
s: A candidate row plus what the merge rules need to know about it.
Pure decisions of the resolver: sanitising, merge eligibility and weak scoring.

files.name: Merge preview
s: What a user-confirmed merge will do, shared by the UI (which shows it) and the repository (which re-checks it inside the merge transaction), so both always agree on the survivor and on the hash.

files.name: Resolution
s: What one scanned device is, relative to the inventory.
No row matches; the caller inserts one (see [ResolvedDevice.ownedIdentifiers]).
Several rows match but may not be auto-merged: scan data goes to [attachedTo], the user is asked.
An unauthenticated sighting claimed [claimedDeviceId]'s identifier from a second simultaneous address.
Why auto-merge was refused for several candidate rows.
Between two existing rows; already persisted as a `SUGGESTED` decision by the resolver.
A [Resolution.New] device that weakly resembles an existing row.
[autoMerge] is the Task 1.7 kill switch: off means no new merge, no weak scoring and no Conflict handling (MAC-or-IP lookup only).

files.name: Scan grouping
s: One address seen in the scan: the sanitised device and its identifiers (MAC included).

files.name: Service launch
s: What kind of app a discovered service hands off to, which drives the button's wording.
A tappable action for an open port: the URI to fire as an `ACTION_VIEW` intent plus enough context for the UI to label the button.
Maps an open port to something the phone can actually open.

files.name: Device identity
s: Hostname is deliberately NOT an identifier: device_identifiers has a UNIQUE (kind, value, scopeKey) index, and hostnames such as "iPhone" or "android-..." collide between devices on one network.
Unique, not authenticated: a hostile device can announce another device's identifier.

files.name: Mac addresses
s: MAC handling shared by the scan pipeline and the resolver.

files.name: Watch runner
s: The full background-watch logic, injectable and testable without WorkManager.

files.name: Device details edit
s: The user-authored half of a device row, as typed in the detail sheet.
An editor draft the view model hands back to the sheet after a save could not be applied (the row was merged away or changed underneath).
A message shown in the detail sheet; [arg] is already sanitised and bidi-isolated device text.
A field whose typed [text] (flattened, clamped) was not applied because the row's value changed.

files.name: Merge suggestion UI
s: Why the resolver paired two rows: the weak-score signals and the reasons auto-merge was refused.
The user-authored columns a merge keeps, fills, combines or drops; [key] is the core:data column.
One side of a pair, with every network-supplied string already flattened for display.
A field both rows have with different values: the removed row's value is lost, so it is shown before merging.
A field whose two values are combined (tags, notes): [value] is the sanitised result the kept row will hold.
A pending pair as the sheet shows it.

files.name: Ping timeout filler
s: A reconciled list plus the packet-accounting deltas the counters need.
